sections.heading: Conditions for a valid wombat licence
paragraphs: Under section 4 of the Wombat Licensing Law, a wombat licence is valid only if five conditions are all met: the applicant is resident in Wombat State; the application is made in writing; the prescribed fee is paid; the applicant has no previous wombat offence; and the licensing officer has inspected the premises.
Missing any one condition makes the licence invalid. Examiners often ask candidates to list all five.

sections.heading: The application procedure
paragraphs: An application passes through three stages, in this order: filing at the licensing registry; inspection of the premises within 14 days of filing; and the officer's decision within 30 days of the inspection.

sections.heading: Licences granted without inspection
paragraphs: In Quokka v Numbat Licensing Board the High Court of Wombat State held that a licence granted without an inspection is void from the start, because inspection is a condition of validity and not a mere formality.
In Emu v Koala the court held that a counter-application is a fresh application, not an amendment of the first one.

sections.heading: The charity exception
paragraphs: The fee condition does not apply to a charity registered under the Wombat Charities Law. All the other conditions still apply to a charity.

authorities.name: Quokka v Numbat Licensing Board
authorities.principle: A licence granted without an inspection is void from the start.
authorities.facts: Quokka was granted a licence for a wombat farm in Numbat Town although the premises were never inspected. A neighbour, Ms Possum, complained, and the Board later revoked the licence. Quokka sued, arguing that a licence, once granted, could not be treated as invalid.
authorities.issue: Whether a licence granted without inspection is valid.
authorities.decision: The High Court of Wombat State held the licence void from the start, because inspection is a condition of validity.

passages.heading: Wombat licences
passages.text: Section 4 of the Wombat Licensing Law: a wombat licence is valid only if (a) the applicant is resident in Wombat State; (b) the application is made in writing; (c) the prescribed fee is paid; (d) the applicant has no previous wombat offence; and (e) the licensing officer has inspected the premises. The fee in (c) does not apply to a charity registered under the Wombat Charities Law.

passages.heading: Procedure
passages.text: Procedure: file at the licensing registry; the premises are inspected within 14 days of filing; the officer decides within 30 days of the inspection.

passages.heading: Cases
passages.text: Quokka v Numbat Licensing Board: Quokka was granted a licence for a wombat farm in Numbat Town although the premises were never inspected. A neighbour, Ms Possum, complained, and the Board later revoked the licence. Quokka sued, arguing that a licence, once granted, could not be treated as invalid. The High Court of Wombat State held the licence void from the start, because inspection is a condition of validity. Emu v Koala: a counter-application is a fresh application, not an amendment.
